column1: # Known differences between scopeio and the reference readers, each checked
# against the TIFF 6.0 specification, the spec-derived truth of tests/data/tiff
# or the raw file bytes. With a tolerance, block means must agree within it
# (lossy data); without, the difference must persist. Tool "scopeio" marks

column4: reason
returns the raw 16-bit half-float bit patterns as uint16; scopeio converts them to f32
10-bit packed samples differ from sample 13 on; scopeio matches the encoded values (MSB first, rows padded to bytes, TIFF 6.0)
lossy JPEG: decoders differ by rounding
lossy JPEG: decoders differ by rounding
no ResolutionUnit tag: TIFF 6.0 defaults to inch (352778 nm for 72 dpi); Bio-Formats reports 13.889 nm
ResolutionUnit 1 (no absolute unit): scopeio reports no pixel size, Bio-Formats assumes micrometres
YCbCr 2x1 data: Bio-Formats colours differ strongly (e.g. raw Y=2 Cb=128 Cr=130 decodes to 184,122,228); scopeio follows TIFF 6.0 section 21 and matches bioformats-rs
YCbCr 2x2 data: Bio-Formats wraps out-of-range values instead of clamping (0 vs 252) and rounds differently
YCbCr 2x2 data: values differ; scopeio follows TIFF 6.0 section 21
Bio-Formats output differs; scopeio matches libtiff (ImageMagick) exactly and Bio-Formats' own result for the tiled copy quad-tile.tif
